correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the full symbolic proof from actual RESULT.md: nonzero fiber F=mA with m>0, A primitive in free lattice. Fiber self-intersection F^2=0 yields integer A^2=0. Compatible almost complex c1(TX,J) is characteristic by c1 mod 2=w2 and Wu, so c1(A) is even; the fiber adjunction c1(F)=2-2g implies 2-2g=m c1(A), hence g-1 multiple of m. Independently confirmed by a stronger earlier theorem: Li-Li Lemma 3.2(1),(3) gives eta(F)=g and eta(mA)=m(eta(A)-1)+1 for square-zero A, again m|(g-1). For genus2 m=1, genus3 m in {1,2}, and g>=3 (g-1) is a multiple of m; the asserted positive-degree conclusions are valid once the contemporary quoted multisection-degree characterization d>=2 iff m|d is granted. No finite computation is used as a universal proof. Source Corollary 8 full text was inaccessible and that conditional cross-reference is a documented limitation, not a contrived scientific FAIL.

originality.rationale: Definitive implication-level coverage by Li and Li (2002), Lemma 3.2(1),(3): applying its general symplectic-genus multiplicity formula to the square-zero connected symplectic Lefschetz fiber F=mA yields g-1=m(eta(A)-1). The submitted entire divisibility theorem is therefore a direct special case of an earlier stronger result, regardless of whether the exact Lefschetz-fibration wording appeared. Its multisection-degree corollaries are arithmetic consequences upon combining this old theorem with the contemporary Baykur-Hamada classification quoted by the submission. Self-index matches excluded. No novel original remainder survives.

value.rationale: The geometry is naturally motivated: fiber-divisibility bounds and low-genus multisection degrees are meaningful, especially for the explicit 2-section question. However, the submission’s entire genus-minus-one divisibility theorem is a direct specialization of Li-Li 2002 Lemma 3.2(1),(3), and each claimed section-degree consequence is a one-line multiple-of-m substitution into the cited 2026 degree theorem. The paper adds neither a new structural lemma nor a non-implied invariant/classification nor a novel solution technique; the attractive low-genus phrasing does not turn this mechanical combination of already established statements into a separate substantive mathematical result. The value FAIL concerns independence of the contribution, not the importance of the surrounding subject.
